title: Introduce Yourself
introduction: Meet someone new, share your name and say that you are a student.
summary: You practised exchanging names and introducing yourself as a student.

media.alt: Visual context for introducing yourself and meeting someone in Yorùbá.

exercises.prompt: You join a community class. Your name is Adé. Choose an introduction so the group knows your name.
exercises.explanation: Orúkọ mi ni ... introduces your name. Here the name is Adé.

exercises.prompt: You have introduced yourself to a new guest. How can you politely ask their name?
exercises.explanation: Kí ni orúkọ yín? asks a person respectfully, or several people, what their name is.

exercises.prompt: At a campus welcome event, someone asks about you. Choose the statement that says you are a student.
exercises.explanation: Mo jẹ́ akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ means I am a student. It adds a little information to your introduction.

exercises.prompt: A new classmate says “Orúkọ mi ni Bádé.” What would be a fitting next step?
options: Introduce yourself with your own name
Offer them food because they said they are hungry
Say good night because they are leaving
exercises.answer: Introduce yourself with your own name
exercises.explanation: Bádé has introduced their name. You can introduce yours with Orúkọ mi ni ...

title: Family & People
introduction: Meet relatives and friends. Practise identifying parents and a younger sibling in a family introduction.
summary: You practised introducing a parent, understanding a sibling relationship and asking who someone’s father is.

media.alt: A mother introducing her family to a visitor at a family gathering.

exercises.prompt: At a family gathering, you are Túndé’s mother and introduce yourself to a visitor. Which statement fits?
exercises.explanation: Èmi ni màmáa Túndé identifies the speaker as Túndé’s mother.

exercises.prompt: You are Kóyè’s father, meeting another parent for the first time. Choose your introduction.
exercises.explanation: Èmi ni bàbáa Kóyè identifies the speaker as Kóyè’s father.

exercises.prompt: Your friend explains a family photo: “Olú ni àbúrò Adé.” What relationship have they described?
exercises.explanation: Àbúrò refers to a younger sibling. This statement identifies Olú as Adé’s younger sibling.

exercises.prompt: You are meeting a friend’s family and want to ask who their father is. Which question fits?
exercises.explanation: Ta ni asks who. Ta ni bàbáà rẹ? asks who your father is.

title: Food & Drink
introduction: At a shared meal, ask for water or rice and recognise a friendly meal wish.
summary: You practised expressing a wish to drink water or eat rice, and wishing someone an enjoyable meal.

media.alt: A host offering water during a shared family meal.

exercises.prompt: After a warm walk, your host asks what you would like. Choose the statement that says you want to drink water.
exercises.explanation: Mo fẹ́ mu omi means I want to drink water. Mu is drink and omi is water.

exercises.prompt: At lunch, rice is available. How do you say you want to eat rice?
exercises.explanation: Mo fẹ́ jẹ ìrẹsì means I want to eat rice. Jẹ is eat and ìrẹsì is rice.

exercises.prompt: Your friend sits down to eat. Choose the expression that wishes them an enjoyable meal.
exercises.explanation: Ẹ kú ìjẹun o! is a meal greeting, similar to enjoy your meal.

exercises.prompt: A guest says “Mo lè mu omi” when you offer water. What have they told you?
exercises.explanation: Mo lè mu omi means I can drink water. Lè expresses can in this sentence.

title: Numbers & Money
introduction: Ask a price and understand small amounts in a practice market exchange.
summary: You practised asking a price, understanding an amount and counting purchases.

media.alt: A learner asking a market seller about the price of peppers.

exercises.prompt: At a market stall, you want to know the price of the peppers in front of you. Which question fits?
exercises.explanation: Eélòó ni ata yìí? asks how much this pepper costs.

exercises.prompt: In a practice price exchange, the seller says “Ogúnun náírà ni.” How much are they asking?
exercises.explanation: Ogúnun náírà ni means it is twenty naira. This is a teaching amount, not a claim about current market prices.

exercises.prompt: You are checking a small practice payment. The seller says “Náírà márùnún”. Which amount should you confirm?
exercises.explanation: Márùnún counts five here: náírà márùnún is five naira.

exercises.prompt: You are buying yams for a family meal. A shopper orders “iṣu mẹ́ta”. How many yams should be packed?
exercises.explanation: Iṣu means yam and mẹ́ta counts three objects. The number follows the noun.

title: Places Around Me
introduction: Recognise useful destinations when planning everyday errands.
summary: You practised identifying a market, school, hospital and toilet in everyday situations.

media.alt: A learner in a local market area identifying where to buy fresh food.

exercises.prompt: You need to buy fresh food for dinner. Which destination would you ask a local friend about?
exercises.explanation: Ọjà means market, a place for buying and selling.

exercises.prompt: You are meeting a teacher where children attend classes. Which destination fits?
exercises.explanation: Ilé-ìwé means school. It identifies your destination, rather than a market.

exercises.prompt: You are accompanying a friend for hospital care. Which place name should you recognise?
exercises.explanation: Ilé ìwòsàn means hospital. This exercise identifies a place, not medical advice.

exercises.prompt: During a visit, you need the toilet. Which facility name should you look for or ask about?
exercises.explanation: Ilé ìgbọnsẹ̀ means toilet.

title: Asking for Directions
introduction: Use familiar landmarks and understand a simple direction or distance clue.
summary: You practised asking about a street, recognising left and understanding distance clues.

media.alt: A learner asking for directions at a street junction near a church.

exercises.prompt: You are walking to a church and reach two streets. Which question asks which street leads there?
options: Títì wo ló lọ sí ṣọ́ọ̀ṣì?
exercises.answer: Títì wo ló lọ sí ṣọ́ọ̀ṣì?
exercises.explanation: Títì wo ló lọ sí ṣọ́ọ̀ṣì? asks which street leads to the church.

exercises.prompt: A local points out the street on “ọwọ́ òsì”. Which side should you follow?
exercises.explanation: Ọwọ́ òsì identifies the left side in this direction.

exercises.prompt: You ask about the market and hear “Ó súnmọ́”. What does this tell you before you set off?
exercises.explanation: Ó súnmọ́ means it is near. It does not tell you opening hours.

exercises.prompt: While discussing two landmarks, your friend uses “jìnnà sí”. Which distance relationship are they describing?
exercises.explanation: Jìnnà sí means far from. Check the distance before deciding how to travel.

title: Transport & Travel
introduction: Discuss getting to a destination and recognise a simple bicycle travel plan.
summary: You practised asking about travel to the market, recognising a bicycle and checking a destination.

media.alt: Two friends discussing how to travel to the market, with transport options visible.

exercises.prompt: You and a friend are planning a market visit. Which question asks how they will get there?
options: Báwo ni o ṣe máa dé ọjà?
exercises.answer: Báwo ni o ṣe máa dé ọjà?
exercises.explanation: Báwo ni o ṣe máa dé ọjà? asks how you will get to the market.

exercises.prompt: Your friend chooses a “kẹ̀kẹ́” for the journey. Which transport are they choosing in this lesson?
exercises.explanation: Kẹ̀kẹ́ means bicycle here. This lesson uses the textbook bicycle sense, not the informal name for a motorised tricycle.

exercises.prompt: A friend mentions an “ìrìn-àjò” while explaining plans to visit another town. What are they talking about?
exercises.explanation: Ìrìn-àjò means journey or travel.

exercises.prompt: Before leaving together, your friend repeats “ọjà” as the destination. Where are you heading?
exercises.explanation: Ọjà means market. Checking the destination helps you plan the trip together.

title: Time & Daily Routine
introduction: Plan your day, recognise a morning meal and talk about tomorrow and bedtime.
summary: You practised future plans, breakfast, tomorrow and saying you want to sleep.

media.alt: Adé preparing to leave home for a visit later in the day.

exercises.prompt: At home in the morning, you are getting ready for a visit later today. Your friend asks whether you will go. Which reply states your plan to go?
exercises.explanation: Mo máa lọ means I will go. Máa marks a future plan; lọ means go.

exercises.prompt: Before leaving for class, your host offers “oúnjẹ àárọ̀”. Which part of your daily routine are they inviting you to?
exercises.explanation: Oúnjẹ àárọ̀ is a morning meal: breakfast. Àárọ̀ refers to the morning.

exercises.prompt: You cannot visit the market today. Your friend suggests “ọ̀la” instead. When should you plan the errand?
exercises.explanation: Ọ̀la means tomorrow. It helps you agree on the day of an upcoming plan.

exercises.prompt: After a busy day, your family asks whether you want another activity. You want to sleep. Which statement explains your wish?
exercises.explanation: Mo fẹ́ sùn means I want to sleep. Fẹ́ expresses a want; sùn means sleep.

title: Shopping & the Market
introduction: Ask what a food seller has, check a price and follow a simple buying exchange.
summary: You practised asking about available food, checking a rice price, understanding a refusal and paying.

media.alt: Adé asking a food seller what meals are available at a Nigerian prepared-food stall with covered serving pots.

exercises.prompt: At a market food stall, you greet the seller and look at the covered serving pots. Before choosing a meal, how do you ask what kinds of food they have?
options: Irú oúnjẹ wo ni ẹ ní?
Báwo ni o ṣe máa dé ọjà?
exercises.answer: Irú oúnjẹ wo ni ẹ ní?
exercises.explanation: Irú oúnjẹ wo ni ẹ ní? asks what kinds of food you have. Ẹ addresses the seller respectfully.

exercises.prompt: You have chosen rice at the stall. Before agreeing to buy it, which question asks how much the seller charges for rice?
options: Eélòó ni ẹ ń ta ìrẹsì?
exercises.answer: Eélòó ni ẹ ń ta ìrẹsì?
exercises.explanation: Eélòó ni ẹ ń ta ìrẹsì? asks how much you are selling rice for. The price-question pattern can be used with the item you want.

exercises.prompt: You offer a lower amount for a meal. The seller answers “Rárá, kò gbà.” What should you understand before continuing?
options: The seller did not accept your offer
exercises.answer: The seller did not accept your offer
exercises.explanation: Rárá, kò gbà rejects the proposed amount: no, that is not acceptable. You have not yet agreed on the price.

exercises.prompt: You and the seller have agreed on the price. You hold out the payment and say “Ẹ gba owó.” What are you asking the seller to do?
exercises.explanation: Ẹ gba owó means take the money, said respectfully when handing over payment.

title: Making Requests
introduction: Ask for something at a food stall, make your request polite and handle a missed explanation.
summary: You practised requesting a dish, saying please, asking for repetition and thanking someone.

media.alt: Adé politely requesting àbùlà from a food seller at an àmàlà and àbùlà food stall.

exercises.prompt: At a food stall, you have chosen àbùlà, the combined stew served with your meal. Which request tells the seller to give you that choice?
exercises.explanation: Ẹ fún mi ní àbùlà requests àbùlà. Ẹ fún mi ní ... is a respectful give me ... pattern.

exercises.prompt: You need an older neighbour’s attention before making a small request. Which expression can you use to say please?
exercises.explanation: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́ means please and can politely introduce a request. Ẹ is respectful.

exercises.prompt: A local gives you directions, but you miss what they say. Which request asks them to say it again?
exercises.explanation: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, tún un sọ means please say it again. Use it when you need to hear an explanation once more.

exercises.prompt: Your neighbour has helped with your request. Which expression politely thanks them before you leave?
exercises.explanation: Ẹ ṣé is a respectful thank you. It acknowledges the help you received.

title: Visual Review
introduction: Connect familiar Yorùbá words with eight images from everyday life. Choose one answer for each image.
summary: You reviewed family, food, places, a direction and travel through eight images.

exercises.prompt: Adé shows you a portrait of his female parent. Which Yorùbá family word identifies her?

media.alt: A smiling woman wearing a patterned outfit and headwrap.

exercises.explanation: Màmá means mother.

exercises.prompt: At a shared meal, which Yorùbá word names the food on this plate?

media.alt: A white plate piled with small cooked white grains.

exercises.explanation: Ìrẹsì means rice.

exercises.prompt: Your host offers this drink with your meal. Which Yorùbá word names it?

media.alt: A clear glass filled with transparent liquid.

exercises.explanation: Omi means water.

exercises.prompt: You are planning to buy fresh food. Which Yorùbá destination matches this scene?

media.alt: An outdoor aisle lined with vendors, produce baskets and colourful umbrellas.

exercises.explanation: Ọjà means market.

exercises.prompt: You accompany a friend to receive medical care. Which Yorùbá place name matches the image?

media.alt: A large building with a red cross and an emergency vehicle outside.

exercises.explanation: Ilé ìwòsàn means hospital.

exercises.prompt: A local points out which side to follow. Which Yorùbá expression matches the direction shown?

media.alt: A person pointing toward the image’s left edge beneath a matching arrow.

exercises.explanation: Ọwọ́ òsì identifies the left side.

exercises.prompt: Your friend chooses this vehicle for a short journey. Which Yorùbá word names it in these lessons?

media.alt: A blue two-wheeled vehicle with pedals, handlebars and a saddle.

exercises.explanation: Kẹ̀kẹ́ names a bicycle in this course.

exercises.prompt: At an àmàlà stall, identify the combined stew served beside the mound in this image. Which choice fits?

media.alt: A plate with a brown mound surrounded by green, yellow and red sauces.

exercises.explanation: Àbùlà is the combined stew you practised requesting at a food stall.

title: Build the Sentence
introduction: Tap the tiles to build each familiar Yorùbá sentence. Tap a selected tile to move it back, then check your answer.
summary: You reviewed eight useful sentences for greetings, introductions, plans and requests.

exercises.prompt: Good morning.
exercises.explanation: Ẹ káàárọ̀

exercises.prompt: My name is Adé.
exercises.explanation: Orúkọ mi ni Adé

exercises.prompt: How much are these peppers?
exercises.explanation: Eélòó ni ata yìí?

exercises.prompt: How will you get to the market?
exercises.explanation: Báwo ni o ṣe máa dé ọjà?

exercises.prompt: I will go.
exercises.explanation: Mo máa lọ

exercises.prompt: I want to sleep.
exercises.explanation: Mo fẹ́ sùn

exercises.prompt: Please say it again.
exercises.explanation: Ẹ jọ̀wọ́, tún un sọ

exercises.prompt: Give me àbùlà.
exercises.explanation: Ẹ fún mi ní àbùlà
